headline: Connecticut adds $12.7 million to heating aid as fuel costs rise
dek: The supplemental state money will support the Connecticut Energy Assistance Program, with deliverable-fuel households able to receive aid together before the winter heating season intensifies.
body: Connecticut is adding $12.7 million in state money to its home-heating assistance program as officials prepare for higher fuel costs and a larger group of households seeking help this winter. Gov. Ned Lamont announced the funding Tuesday from the state’s Federal Cuts Response Fund, saying it will supplement federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program dollars flowing through the Connecticut Energy Assistance Program, or CEAP. The [governor’s announcement](https://portal.ct.gov/governor/news/press-releases/2026/10-2026/governor-lamont-releases-state-aid-for-home-heating-assistance) identifies the money as supplemental aid for the 2026–27 season.

The immediate effect is for households that use deliverable fuels such as heating oil, kerosene or propane. Connecticut Social Services Commissioner Andrea Barton Reeves said the added funding will let eligible deliverable-fuel households receive their CEAP benefits at the same time rather than waiting until one benefit is exhausted before accessing another. That timing matters in a state where a family can face a large fuel delivery bill before the coldest part of winter, particularly when the household has little room in its budget for a sudden price increase.

The state’s approved federal fiscal-year 2027 plan anticipates serving about 94,291 Connecticut households, including roughly 32,893 households using deliverable fuel, according to the governor’s office. The program gives priority to households with someone age 60 or older, a child younger than 6, or a person with a disability. Connecticut officials told [WFSB](https://www.wfsb.com/2026/10/13/state-releases-millions-additional-heating-aid-winter-approaches/) that the assistance program has about $73 million in federal LIHEAP funding and that roughly 10,000 additional households are now eligible, bringing the statewide total above 94,000.

That larger caseload is arriving alongside a sharper cost problem. WFSB reported that heating oil was more than $2.50 per gallon higher than a year earlier and that electric costs had also risen. The station reported that state officials do not consider the $12.7 million sufficient to cover the entire shortfall, and that federal dollars will be used before the state draws on additional money. The state says about $250.6 million will remain in the Federal Cuts Response Fund after this proposal, but the amount available is not the same as money already committed to heating aid.

CEAP applications for the 2026–27 season are already open. The [Department of Social Services program page](https://portal.ct.gov/DSS/Economic-Security/Winter-Heating-Assistance/Energy-Assistance---Winter-Heating?language=en-US) lists benefit amounts of $355 to $705, depending on household size, income and heating source. It says benefits are generally paid directly to a utility or fuel vendor, and that eligible deliverable-fuel households may qualify for additional deliveries, payment-matching plans, shut-off protection and heating-equipment repairs or replacement.

Income eligibility is based on annual gross income at or below 60% of Connecticut’s state median income. For federal fiscal year 2027, the governor’s office lists $93,681 for a family of four; households receiving certain means-tested benefits, including SNAP, Temporary Family Assistance or Supplemental Security Income, may qualify through categorical rules. Eligibility is determined through the program, so the income threshold should not be treated as an automatic award amount.

Residents can apply online at [ct.gov/heatinghelp](https://ct.gov/heatinghelp), through their local community action agency by phone, email or mail, or by appointment in person. Connecticut says applicants should apply each year rather than assume a prior CEAP award carries over. People who need help locating the right agency can call 2-1-1. The first day for program-paid fuel deliveries is Nov. 2, 2026, and the application deadline for this heating season is May 31, 2027.

The funding is a response to an immediate affordability squeeze, not a guarantee that every household facing a larger bill will be covered. [WSHU reported](https://www.wshu.org/connecticut-news/2026-10-13/ct-low-income-energy-assistance-heat-winter) earlier Tuesday that Lamont had warned of a possible steep increase in home-heating costs and planned to seek help from the state reserve. The new announcement supplies a specific amount and application path; the unresolved questions are how prices will move through winter, how many eligible households ultimately apply and whether Connecticut will need to commit more state or federal resources.
location: Connecticut statewide, with the program administered from Hartford
author: NorthEast News Desk
